commits.subject: Docs: overview and order_status doc blocks, persist_docs on marts; microbatch runs one batch at a time

lines: +      # write the descriptions into the database as COMMENTs (tables and columns)
# after each mart is built, refresh the optimizer statistics of the new table
+This project turns the raw data of the Jaffle Shop (schemas `jaffle_shop` and `stripe`)
+into tested, documented tables for the finance and marketing teams.
+- **staging**: one model per raw table, light cleaning only (rename, cast, cents to dollars)
+- **intermediate**: reusable building blocks (private to the finance group)
+Built with dbt Core 1.11 on DuckDB while studying for the dbt Analytics Engineering Certification.
+| placed         | The order is placed but not yet paid or shipped           |
+| shipped        | The order has been shipped to the customer                |
+| completed      | The order has been received by the customer               |
+| return_pending | The customer asked to return the order                    |
+| returned       | The order has been returned and refunded                  |
description: Total of the successful payments, in dollars (0 when not paid yet).
rows of fct_order_items whose event_time is inside the batch.
A normal run re-processes the current batch and 1 previous batch (lookback).
+-- concurrent_batches=False: run the batches one after the other. Since Chapter 20,
+-- persist_docs writes a COMMENT ON TABLE in every batch; on DuckDB, batches that
